added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite gate log (both keys absent), so an added-failure count could not be derived from the reviewed run's own arms. The reviewed run's declared gate (ruff check --no-cache --output-format=concise reckon/crew/promotion.py -> 3 findings, no PERF401; and the two named suites 10 passed EXIT=0) was independently reproduced by this review against the reviewed head 5f89f2a93, and the base arm was reproduced by running the same ruff command over the base revision 87f6c16a of the same file, which reports the same three findings plus the PERF401 at line 8710 the change removes.

item_verdicts.call_sites: store_committed_review has exactly one production call site, promotion.py:8710, and the change alters only how its return value is collected, not how it is called.
item_verdicts.diff: Read; the sole commit 5f89f2a93 ('lint(crew): build committed review paths with list.extend') replaces `for payload in committed_review_payloads: committed_review_paths.append(review_module.store_committed_review(payload, project=project, root=ledger_root))` with `committed_review_paths.extend(review_module.store_committed_review(payload, project=project, root=ledger_root) for payload in committed_review_payloads)`. Evaluation order and the per-payload store side effect are unchanged, and partial appends on a mid-iteration ValueError are preserved (verified empirically), so the rollback path that restores already-written paths behaves identically.
item_verdicts.done_when: Not stated as an explicit done-when in the reviewed manifest; the operative goal is the removal of the added lint finding. I reproduced the measurement the manifest calls for: ruff check --no-cache --output-format=concise reckon/crew/promotion.py at head 5f89f2a93 reports exactly UP035 (line 15), UP017 (line 4330) and PERF403 (line 6869), no PERF401; the same command over the base revision 87f6c16a reports those three plus PERF401 (line 8710), so the changed source path gains no finding and loses exactly the one.
item_verdicts.goal: The node's goal is to remove the one lint finding the prior review of r-20261006T162208732004 flagged on this work: a PERF401 at promotion.py:8710, raised by the for-loop that appended one stored review-record path per payload in the promotion's review-round store loop added by the plan's section 3 work. The commit converts that loop to a single list.extend over a generator, which is exactly the fix PERF401 prescribes; ruff on reckon/crew/promotion.py at the reviewed head reports three findings and no PERF401, against four findings including the PERF401 at base.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read; its changed_paths [reckon/crew/promotion.py] match the diff exactly, its commits list the single commit 5f89f2a93, its status is complete, and its tests field records the ruff command plus the two named suites at 10 passed EXIT=0, all of which I reproduced.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The reviewed run's declared write paths are reckon/crew/promotion.py and two evidence paths under docs/evidence/fragments and docs/figures; git diff --name-only 87f6c16a..5f89f2a93 lists only reckon/crew/promotion.py, entirely inside the declaration, with nothing added outside it and no evidence fragment needed for a one-line lint fix.

justifications.durability: The refactor is behaviour-preserving: the generator stores each payload eagerly and list.extend appends progressively, so a ValueError raised on one record leaves the already-written paths in committed_review_paths and the _restore_landing_writes rollback runs unchanged (confirmed by running the append-loop and extend forms against a raising generator, both leaving [10, 20]). The change is not itself guarded by an assertion that no PERF401 returns, so it rests on the repo's lint gate rather than a test; small and correct, but the extend-atomicity assumption is load-bearing and untested.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced both halves of the manifest's claim against the reviewed tree: ruff at head reports three findings and no PERF401, ruff at base reports four including PERF401 at 8710, and the two named suites pass 10 EXIT=0 (tests/test_every_review_round_is_committed.py + tests/test_review_record_committed_at_promotion.py). I also verified empirically that list.extend over a generator preserves the items yielded before a mid-iteration ValueError, so the reviewed change's exception-path behaviour matches the append loop it replaces.
justifications.fit: The one-call collection drops into the same lines, indentation and surrounding comment, introduces no abstraction, no plan or stage label, no version suffix and no attribution, and the conventional subject with a body explains the mechanism (eager store, rollback unchanged).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The change does precisely what the node exists to do: it eliminates the PERF401 that the prior review of r-20261006T162208732004 flagged by adopting the exact idiom that rule prescribes (list.extend over a generator), touching only the flagged loop and nothing else in the review-round store path.
justifications.reuse: It reuses the builtin list.extend over the existing store_committed_review generator instead of adding a helper or a second collection step, which is the minimal and idiomatic form for this transformation.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 87f6c16a..5f89f2a93 lists exactly one path, reckon/crew/promotion.py, matching the manifest's changed_paths and inside the declared write scope; nothing outside is touched and no evidence fragment is added for a small lint fix.
